class: Any catalogue template whose RENDERED text is stored in the database and later read back by matching it against the template's fixed words (restore_explanation) is orphaned by a wording change: every row stored before the change no longer fits, and a reader that skips unreadable rows hides them silently (no error, no 500, the list is just shorter). A wording pass over the catalogue therefore deletes history from the user's view unless the earlier text stays readable.
mechanism: GC-IC1 step 7 (#629 wording, merged e1f1ec0a on feature/adjustments) changed paper_alert_title from 'Paper strategy - {name}' to 'Paper strategy — {name}'. restore_explanation (backend/ofo/errors/explanations.py:2023) builds its regex from the CURRENT text only; _alerts_out (backend/ofo_app/routes/paper.py:874-886) catches the ValueError per row, logs 'paper alert N left out: stored text fits no alert template' and drops the row.

fix: Class-level, merged 8abeb451 on feature/adjustments (b69a610d): RESTORED_FORMER_TEXTS (template id -> earlier texts, read-back only, never rendered) tried by restore_explanation after the current text; seeded with the pre-step-7 title. Stored rows are history and keep the words they were written with. Real-data proof (the 5 ofo_dev alerts shown by GET /paper/alerts) owed at the next API start.
